attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Auxiliary variables can shrink deterministic representations.
attacks.method: Forget auxiliaries and target ordinary DNNF rather than d-DNNF.
attacks.notes: The H016 lesson is incorporated.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: AND gates may combine overlapping variable supports.
attacks.method: Determine whether H041 certificates force separators or allow unrestricted overlap.
attacks.notes: This exact overlap question decides whether the bridge is true.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Polytope communication lower bounds often encode full optimization, while the lifts assert only feasibility.
attacks.method: Use witness recovery to define a search relation rather than a full slack matrix.
attacks.notes: Whether recovery suffices for a strong protocol is the central gate.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Encode information in coefficients.
attacks.method: Charge polynomial bit length and include coefficient transmission in protocol cost.
attacks.notes: The formulation blocks infinite-precision hiding.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: The target may not be a tautology.
attacks.method: Retain the conditional clause and link the gate explicitly to H026.
attacks.notes: The route cannot advance beyond target selection until H026 is settled.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Recursive extensions may efficiently simulate the bounded-depth proof lower bound target.
attacks.method: Search for explicit short extension-PC proofs of weaker variants.
attacks.notes: No such proof family or lower bound is known for the exact candidates.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Random formulas do not give the required polynomial-time explicit family.
attacks.method: Demand a deterministic generator or a verified seed search with asymptotic proof.
attacks.notes: Explicitness is the primary missing gate.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Eliminating XOR variables may simplify the non-affine gadget unexpectedly.
attacks.method: Track expansion and clause width under every allowed substitution.
attacks.notes: No closure theorem or collapsing substitution has been found.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: A hard family may depend on the policy and fail polynomial-time uniformity.
attacks.method: Allow the constructor polynomial access to the fixed policy description but require uniform output.
attacks.notes: Policy-relative explicitness is coherent for each fixed policy.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: CDCL with restarts can simulate general resolution.
attacks.method: Separate existence of a short resolution proof from the time a fixed deterministic policy needs to discover it.
attacks.notes: Simulation power alone does not refute search lower bounds.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Existing range-avoidance hardness may be conditional or for restricted circuits.
attacks.method: Match the exact circuit class and oracle access in the reduction.
attacks.notes: A general-circuit unconditional hardness premise remains missing.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Arbitrary infinite NP sets may not yield efficiently indexed avoidance instances.
attacks.method: Require witnesses and length-padding to be explicit in the reduction.
attacks.notes: No universal encoding theorem or counterexample is currently registered.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Negative SAT answers lack NP witnesses.
attacks.method: Use self-reducible formula pairs or proof-carrying range instances to avoid uncertified coNP claims.
attacks.notes: The bridge survives only as an explicit unresolved certificate-design problem.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Range avoidance may produce lower bounds for exponential-time classes rather than SAT.
attacks.method: Audit whether the reduction targets SAT circuits of each fixed polynomial size.
attacks.notes: Existing range-avoidance consequences do not automatically give the desired SAT anti-checker.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Invoke SETH to reject nontrivial Circuit-SAT algorithms.
attacks.method: Check whether SETH covers arbitrary polynomial-size circuits rather than k-CNF.
attacks.notes: SETH is not the exact negation and remains an assumption.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: A lower bound for NEXP or restricted circuits need not imply P != NP.
attacks.method: Record the route as intermediate unless it reaches an NP language.
attacks.notes: The hypothesis advances circuit lower bounds but is not a standalone proof of P != NP.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Polynomial time in the truth-table length is exponential in input length and may be too weak.
attacks.method: State complexity consistently in truth-table length and track uniform generation of the NP family.
attacks.notes: The property is a circuit-lower-bound object, not yet an efficient input algorithm.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Pseudorandom functions may still rule out sparse properties under stronger assumptions.
attacks.method: Check whether standard natural-proofs arguments require largeness.
attacks.notes: The classical theorem does not directly exclude exponentially sparse properties.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: A linear-map lower bound does not itself separate P from NP.
attacks.method: Treat it as method development and require explicit transfer lessons to H058/H030.
attacks.notes: It is retained only as a barrier-breaking laboratory target.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Boolean and arithmetic linear circuit models differ.
attacks.method: Require each sharpened descendant to choose one model, field, and cost convention.
attacks.notes: The current disjunction is a frontier map; formal proof attempts must split it.
